plan_identifier_systems.description: The Federated Plan Identifier (f_plan_id). Where the FPI identifies the contracting legal payer entity, the f_plan_id identifies one specific plan entry published by that payer. It MUST be a randomly generated UUIDv4 in canonical lowercase hyphenated form, and MUST NOT be derived from any plan attribute, so it never encodes plan name, contract ID, or any other plan metadata. Each f_plan_id MUST be unique within a Payer Well-Known Endpoint File and MUST remain stable over time, including across plan years, even when the plan's name, website, endpoints, or source identifier value change. A new f_plan_id is minted only for a plan that has not previously been published, and an f_plan_id belonging to a retired plan is never reused for a different plan. Because the value is random it cannot be recomputed the way an FPI can, so its stability depends entirely on the publisher carrying forward the value it previously published; tooling in this repository does this through load_existing_f_plan_ids() in tools/seed_medicare_advantage/seed.py. Every plan identifier also carries parent_fpi, naming the FPI of the payer legal entity that owns the plan. This is an early exploratory prototype and should not be considered a formal or permanent identification system.

plan_identifier_systems.acronym: CMS Medicare Advantage Contract ID and Plan ID
plan_identifier_systems.description: A specific Medicare Advantage, Part D, Cost Plan, PACE, or other CMS plan benefit package, identified by the CMS contract number together with the plan (benefit package) number within that contract. The value is the CMS contract ID and the plan ID joined by a single hyphen, for example 'H1234-432'. The contract portion is the alphanumeric contract number CMS assigns to the organization operating the plan, which is the CMS_CONTRACT_ID payer identifier system, and the plan portion is the three-digit plan benefit package number assigned within that contract. Contract numbers identify contracts rather than payer legal entities, so it is a plan's parent_fpi, and never its contract number, that names the owning payer entity. Plan segment IDs, which further subdivide a plan benefit package by service area, are not part of this identifier value.
